join_order.notes: Bitmap on custkey (187KB, fits L1). Filter orders by bitmap + o_orderdate.
Use lineitem_l_orderkey_grouped index. Sort qualifying orderkeys first for sequential lineitem access.

qualifying_orders.notes: CRITICAL: Use compact arrays sized to number of qualifying orders (~3.5M), NOT max_orderkey (~60M). Per-thread collection then merge. This replaces the old approach of 4 separate arrays each sized to max_orderkey (~60M entries totaling ~1GB).

aggregation.notes: For each qualifying order, compute revenue sum inline during lineitem probe. Store result directly in the compact qualifying_orders array (add a double revenue field). No separate aggregation map needed since each qualifying orderkey is unique.

parallelism.orders_scan: static partitioning of orders rows, per-thread compact arrays, then merge
parallelism.lineitem_probe: dynamic scheduling over sorted qualifying orderkeys (chunk size ~4096). Each order's lineitems are contiguous, so threads process non-overlapping orderkey ranges. Revenue accumulated directly into the compact result array — no atomics needed since each orderkey appears exactly once.
parallelism.notes: Sort qualifying orderkeys before lineitem probe to ensure sequential access pattern across lineitem columns (sorted by l_orderkey). This maximizes prefetch and cache line utilization.

indexes.purpose: O(1) lookup of contiguous lineitem rows per qualifying orderkey

optimization_notes: Category C — Work Elimination. Root cause: the iter_0 code allocated 4 arrays indexed by max_orderkey (~60M), totaling ~1GB of zero-initialized memory, but only ~3.5M entries were used. This allocation+initialization dominated runtime (593ms total vs ~55ms in measured phases). Fix: replace all max_orderkey-sized arrays with compact arrays sized to the number of qualifying orders (~3.5M). Store (orderkey, orderdate, shippriority, revenue) in a single compact struct array. Sort qualifying orderkeys before lineitem probe for sequential access. Fuse aggregation into the probe loop — since each orderkey is unique among qualifying orders, accumulate revenue directly into the compact array slot. This reduces memory from ~1GB to ~56MB and eliminates the initialization bottleneck.
